title: AirAsia 8501 Ascended, Then Stalled Before Crash

image.attribution: Jyi1693 at en.wikipedia / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
Aviation officials in Indonesia say an AirAsia Flight 8501 that crashed into the Java Sea last month ascended steeply, then stalled and hurtled toward the sea, with the co-pilot at the controls.

In a news conference Thursday, investigators from Indonesia’s National Transportation Safety Committee said the plane’s voice recorder indicated that the Airbus A-320’s “stall” warning came on during the plane’s ascent and continued until it made impact with the water.

It also indicated that co-pilot French national Remi Emmanuel Plesel, who has about 6,000 flight hours, was at the controls when the plane went down. Indonesian pilot Iryanto with some 20,000 flight hours, was monitoring the flight.

All 162 people aboard the plane died when it crashed on December 28. Divers have recovered 70 bodies from the wreckage.

The flight was en route from Surabaya, Indonesia’s second-largest city, to Singapore when it went down.

Rescue and recovery operations were hampered by rough seas and poor visibility. The plane’s flight date recorders, or “black boxes,” were located two weeks ago.

questions.question: How did officials describe the last minutes of flight 8501?
options: The plane initially leveled off before descending rapidly.
The aircraft maintained a steady altitude before stalling.
The flight ascended sharply and then stalled before crashing.
The pilots executed emergency maneuvers to stabilize the flight.
questions.answer: The flight ascended sharply and then stalled before crashing.

questions.question: Who was controlling the plane at the moment of the crash?
options: The lead pilot, Iryanto, was at the controls.
Co-pilot Remi Emmanuel Plesel was flying the plane.
An automated system took over the flight.
Both pilots shared control of the aircraft equally.
questions.answer: Co-pilot Remi Emmanuel Plesel was flying the plane.

questions.question: How many bodies were recovered up to this moment?
options: 50 bodies have been found and identified.
70 bodies have been recovered from the wreckage.
100 bodies were initially recovered after the crash.
All bodies have been recovered from the sea.
questions.answer: 70 bodies have been recovered from the wreckage.
